hook.line: At the café, somebody always asks who can do what: who is good with the oven, who can carry fifty chairs, who can say no to a regular. English uses "good at" and "able to" for all of it, but Spanish has a different phrase for a natural knack, a general skill and one particular act.
hook.es: A Vale se le dan muy bien los postres.
hook.en: Vale is very good at desserts.

examples.es: Soy capaz de correr diez kilómetros.
examples.en: I'm able to run ten kilometres.

examples.es: No fui capaz de decirle la verdad.
examples.en: I wasn't able to tell him the truth.

examples.es: A Vale se le dan muy bien los postres.
examples.en: Vale is very good at desserts.

examples.es: A Tomás no se le dan bien los números.

rule:
Three ways to talk about ability.

*Se me da bien* + infinitive or noun: a natural knack. The person is the one "given" the skill: *me*, *te*, *le*. With a plural noun, *da* becomes *dan*: *no se le dan bien los números*.

*Soy bueno para* + noun or infinitive: a general skill you have built up. A woman says *buena*.

*Ser capaz de* + infinitive: being able to do one particular, often hard, thing. In the past it can mean you managed it, or you could not bring yourself to: *No fui capaz de decírselo*.

The three are not interchangeable. A knack is not an achievement.
smallPrint: Teachers call *se me da bien* a construction with an indirect object, like *me gusta*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the phrase: *___ cocinar.* (*Se me da bien* or *Soy capaz de*) Say: I'm good at cooking.
yourTurn.why: A natural knack takes *se me da bien*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the phrase: *___ correr diez kilómetros.* (*Se me da bien* or *Soy capaz de*) Say: I'm able to run ten kilometres.
yourTurn.answer: Soy capaz de correr diez kilómetros.
yourTurn.why: One specific hard thing takes *ser capaz de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm good at maths.
yourTurn.why: A general skill takes *ser bueno para*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I wasn't able to tell him the truth.
yourTurn.answer: No fui capaz de decirle la verdad.
yourTurn.why: One moment where you could not do it takes *no fui capaz de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Vale is very good at desserts.
yourTurn.answer: A Vale se le dan muy bien los postres.
yourTurn.why: The person goes after *a*, and plural *postres* makes it *se le dan*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Tomás isn't good with numbers.
yourTurn.answer: A Tomás no se le dan bien los números.
yourTurn.why: The noun is plural, so *da* becomes *dan*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it as a knack: *Soy bueno para cocinar.* Say: I'm good at cooking.
yourTurn.why: Swap *soy bueno para* for *se me da bien*; the infinitive stays.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish does not say "be good in"; use *se me da bien* or *soy bueno para*.

pitfalls.wrong: Se me da bien las matemáticas.
pitfalls.right: Se me dan bien las matemáticas.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The thing you are good at is the subject, so a plural noun needs *dan*.

pitfalls.wrong: Soy capaz en correr diez kilómetros.
pitfalls.right: Soy capaz de correr diez kilómetros.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Ser capaz* always joins the next verb with *de*.

personal: Say one thing that comes naturally to you with *Se me da bien…*, and one hard thing you did once with *Fui capaz de…*
